status: FROZEN 2026-11-06: the user approved the expected plans; the SHA-256 is recorded as PLANS_SHA256 in gold_plans.py
rules: A case-run passes when the final plan matches every expected field: needs_numbers, needs_text, needs_sentiment, include_chart, clarify (a clarification question is asked) and the set of metrics (metric, dimension).
When clarify is expected true, only clarify is compared: the other fields are not used when Echo asks first.

hard: the case must pass in every repeat. Hard cases are P1 (the question of live runs 63-66) and the cases marked hard here (P10, P11), which exist to test that no clarification is asked (P2_DECISION_CRITERIA_v2, M3).
validator: the expected value of a field follows from a code normalization, not from a model decision; it is still compared, and the label marks it in review.
Expected plans are written from the manager's point of view, not from the planning prompt.

cases.question: I'm preparing for a team check-in. Using all eligible anonymous Recognition survey comments for the third quarter of 2026, classify each comment as positive, negative, neutral, mixed, or indeterminate. Show the count and percentage in each category, including the denominator. Include a short literal excerpt illustrating a positive and a critical view if available, with source citations. Explain the main patterns and interpretation limits, and suggest two follow-up questions for the team. Base this analysis on comment text rather than numerical survey ratings, and do not identify respondents.
cases.why: The question of live runs 63-66 (run 64 added numbers and a chart; 65 and 66 asked for clarification). Counts come from the sentiment classification, not from SQL.

cases.question: What is the overall sentiment of the Workload survey comments this quarter?
cases.why: Sentiment only, short form. Counts come from the classification, not from survey ratings; no SQL.

cases.question: How did the Recognition favorable score change across the first three quarters of 2026?
cases.why: Numeric only: survey ratings, no comments.

cases.question: Show me a chart of the Manager support and Workload survey scores over the first three quarters of 2026.
cases.why: Chart requested; one survey_trend per topic.

cases.question: How many cross-team contributions did my team make this quarter?
cases.why: Numeric, chart not requested; catalog metric with dimension null.

cases.question: Give me two short quotes from the Team climate comments that show what people value about the team.
cases.why: Comment examples without a sentiment classification. Not covered by a planning rule written for runs 63-66.

cases.question: Has Recognition improved over the first three quarters of 2026, and what do the Recognition comments say about the reasons?
cases.why: Numbers and text together; comments are interpreted, not classified.

cases.question: I'm preparing for a team check-in. Has recognition improved over the first three quarters of 2026? How does that compare with how supported people feel by their managers? Show me a simple table of the results, explain the main changes, and tell me what I should be careful about when interpreting them.
cases.why: The offline MEDIUM_QUESTION. A table is not a chart; explaining numbers does not need comment text.

cases.question: Which work requests assigned to my team had the most rework hours this quarter?
cases.why: Custom SQL over Rework_Hours: no catalog metric, so metrics=[]. The metrics rule covers the empty list; what it does not cover is choosing SQL over a catalog metric.

cases.question: What are my people saying about workload this quarter?
cases.why: Must not ask for clarification: team and dates are fixed by the application; the comments are retrieved by Vanilla. It asks what the comments say (interpretation), not a classification of every comment, so needs_sentiment=false.

cases.question: Summarize the eNPS results for my teams for Q3 2026.
cases.why: Must not ask for clarification: the survey data is retrieved by Cherry, not supplied by the manager. eNPS is a survey dimension; the scope is Q3 only (default scope).

cases.question: Compare it with what we discussed in our last meeting.
cases.why: Must ask: 'it' and the earlier meeting are not available to any permitted tool.

cases.question: Is it getting better or worse?
cases.why: Must ask: the subject of the question is missing.

cases.question: Classify the sentiment of the Recognition comments this quarter and plot the results.
cases.why: Chart requested over sentiment counts, which come from Vanilla. The current architecture requires numbers for a chart, so honoring it would send Cherry an unrequested numeric task (run 64 exhausted the budget this way). include_chart=false is the code normalization, not a judgment that no chart is needed. needs_numbers stays false; accepting true would test a different and worse plan. The missing chart of sentiment counts is a known product gap.
